**The Opportunity**
 The Connect team is building an integrations platform from scratch. Most integration platforms require hand\-written code for each connector. Connect takes a declarative approach: you define connectors as structured specifications, and the platform validates and executes them. Product teams embed integrations through an SDK. End users access them through a separate gateway. The platform handles credential management, execution, and reliability for both paths.
   

  

 As a Software Engineer on this team, you will spend most of your time in the backend: implementing connectors as declarative specs, building services that talk to third\-party APIs, and working on the platform infrastructure that makes those integrations reliable. The problems are real and varied: OAuth flows that differ across every provider, webhooks that arrive out of order, rate limits that change without notice.
   

  

 You will also build features in the React and TypeScript frontend. The admin product serves internal operators, and the interfaces you build need to be production\-quality. You will carry features from API to interface without a handoff.
   

  

 Expect a split of roughly 70% backend and 30% frontend , stable over time. The role suits engineers who want to grow their backend skills on real infrastructure problems, are comfortable working across the stack, and care about shipping well\-built software.

 Day\-to\-day work falls into the areas below. Backend platform work carries most of the weight; frontend work serves the systems you build.
   

  

* Build connectors and platform services. Implement integrations as declarative specs and build the backend services that execute them. Each new connector teaches you something about how third\-party APIs actually behave.
* Handle the realities of third\-party APIs. Work with OAuth flows, webhook ingestion, rate limiting, and retries. Learn to debug failures in systems the team does not control.
* Write code that handles state carefully. Work with connection management, sync state, and workflow execution where correctness matters more than speed.
* Contribute across the stack. Build features end to end, including the React and TypeScript frontend, and keep frontend patterns coherent as the product matures.
* Participate in technical decisions. Contribute to design discussions, ask good questions about tradeoffs, and develop your judgment for when simple solutions outperform clever ones.
* Grow through ownership. Take on well\-scoped projects, deliver them end to end, and expand your scope as you build confidence with the platform.
* Collaborate closely with a small team. Engage in code reviews and design discussions, give and receive feedback, and help the team maintain high engineering quality.

**Job Description**
 The Cardiovascular Biomechanics Computation Lab at Stanford University, led by Dr. Alison Marsden, specializes in computational modeling of the cardiovascular system to advance surgical planning, medical device design, and fundamental research in biomechanics. The lab develops SimVascular, a leading open\-source project for patient\-specific modeling and blood flow simulation, and is actively creating tools for segmentation and virtual surgery in 3D Slicer.
   

  

 The lab has a particular interest in congenital heart disease patients, and we are leading a national collaborative effort to develop software for anatomic modeling, virtual surgery, and simulations pertaining to this patient group, with the ultimate goal of achieving FDA approval and clinical translation.

* Implementing quality control in code development
* Performing code profiling and improving efficiency

* Implementing new GPU acceleration capabilities
* Reviewing and providing feedback on solver contributions from Marsden lab members and partner labs
* Overseeing and collaborating on web\-based documentation development
* Participating in long term strategic planning with Dr. Marsden, the lab’s Senior Software Research Engineer and others in the national collaborative
